newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway government non-committal on bank merger.
newsitem.headline: Norway government non-committal on bank merger.

text.p: Norwegian Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg on Wednesday declined to give his opinion on the proposed merger between Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA and insurer Storebrand ASA.
Under Norwegian law, the Finance Ministry as regulator authority has the final say in mergers between financial institutions.
Stoltenberg said during question time in parliament it was important to look into all aspects of the proposed fusion before making a decision.

"It would therefore be wrong of me to give any signals at this stage on what the government wants to do," he said. "Among the things we are looking at is what importance a possible merger would have for domestic competition."
Christiania, Norway's second largest bank, and Storebrand, the country's top insurer, would become the largest financial group in Norway and the sixth biggest in the Nordic region.
The companies hope to win acceptance for their proposal at their respective annual general meetings at the end of April, followed by possible regulatory approval in June.
The merger would be completed at the end of the year and the new group be named Christiania.
